content: 1. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments as directed by your healthcare provider. 2. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. 3. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. 4. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. 5. This information was last revised in May 2024. 6. This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. 7. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. 8. Amoxicillin is used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections. It belongs to the penicillin class of antibiotics and is effective only against bacterial infections. It will not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. 9. Take this medication orally as directed by your doctor, typically once daily, within one hour of finishing a meal. Swallow the tablets whole; do not crush or chew them. 10. For optimal effectiveness, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. 11. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. 12. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. 13. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection (fungal infections). 14. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. 15. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. Amoxicillin can commonly cause a mild rash, which is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish this from a rare rash that could indicate a severe allergic reaction. 16. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. 17. Before taking amoxicillin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to penicillin or cephalosporin antibiotics, or if you have any other allergies. 18. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. 19. Amoxicillin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. 20. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Amoxicillin passes into breast milk. 21. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. 22. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 23. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as specific diabetic urine tests, potentially causing false test results. 24. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. 25. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. 26. With prolonged treatment, laboratory and/or medical tests (such as kidney and liver function tests or complete blood counts) may be conducted while you are taking this medication. 27. Always keep all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled.
